parsed.explanation: Combined regime: national passport sex-marker restriction is in force (Supreme Court allowed it Nov 2025), so mismatched visitor documents can be refused at entry, and the cable permits a lifetime fraud-ineligibility finding. Facility bans cover government buildings in about 19 states, with criminal trespass in 4, and a documented arrest held a trans woman in a men's ward. Immigration and corrections custody show documented sexual abuse, forced labour and birth-sex-style placement. Protections exist (national hate-crime and employment law, marriage, 22 states plus DC anti-discrimination), but they are partly enjoined, and the state/province minor-care ban and state violence record add exposure. Violence counts lack denominators and the 4.8/100k figure is an undercount floor, so no trans-specific violence rate is assessed. No execution pathway is documented; severity is major-to-severe, not catastrophic.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports issued as M/F by birth sex; discrepancies trigger refusal and request for evidence; confiscation and blocking reported; fraud ground could yield lifetime ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; some restrictions challenged in court; the lifetime bar is not automatic and has waiver options.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry leads to refusal or fraud review, which can escalate into stranding or a permanent bar.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented arrest for restroom use (trespass, up to 60 days). Held 24 hours in men's ward. Immigration custody: forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse reported. Federal corrections adopted conversion-style policies and stopped reporting trans prisoner counts.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Pretrial release was granted in the restroom case; the trespass offence requires willful entry plus refusal to leave, not automatic arrest.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility rules at state level feed into birth-sex placement; a federal custody regime then carries the harm forward.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Government-building facility bans in about 19 states (K-12 and colleges included); 6 states extend to some private settings; 4 states criminalise certain restroom use.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states, 4 territories and DC have no such ban in mapped categories; other sex-definition laws may still apply.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal sex definition reinforces state bans. A visitor in a restricted state faces facility exposure without a local remedy.

care_services.exposure: State bans minors' care. A coastal hospital cancelled adult gender-affirming surgery in Feb 2025 (at least three patients affected). Federal proposed rules and subpoenas of hospital records target youth care.
care_services.protection: State employee health plan settlement covers medically necessary care for dependents; this is a resident-facing route and not a visitor protection.
care_services.interaction: Funding decisions made outside the state narrow adult surgical access; a visitor seeking care may be refused at a hospital.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups as targets; a cash-reward system for leadership of such groups; executive orders call for prosecuting teachers who facilitate social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy states powers will not target people who merely disagree; the referenced orders have partly been enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing raises the stakes for any visible trans advocacy or activity; a traveller is not the primary target but is exposed to the framing.

minors_guardians.exposure: State bans minors' hormone therapy and surgery inside the state (licence revocation). Travelling minors cannot obtain transition care from a licensed clinician there. Federal school-prosecution orders and proposed insurance rules add exposure for guardians.
minors_guardians.protection: Minors already on hormones before 1 July 2023 may continue. Plan coverage can reach minors' care obtained out of state.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor needing care in the state faces a legal bar; a guardian's document or records mismatch could also trigger entry refusal.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police reported three violent crimes against trans women in one major city in 2023 and described violence as epidemic-level. No denominator; the 4.8/100k rate is an undercount floor and is not used.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Investigations were opened; outcomes not recorded. National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; only 23 states have state bias statutes covering it.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse exists in principle, but state-level coverage is partial and documented case outcomes are absent.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport, facility and custody policies are in force or partly in effect; the state minor-care ban's enforceability is unverified; the hospital suspension's permanence is unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined several orders; the passport challenge is pending; no sodomy law nationally; national employment and hate-crime protections; same-sex marriage recognised nationally.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Outcomes depend on which measures are active at the time of travel; remedies are slow and partial.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: birth-sex custody placement with documented harm, plus cross-dressing or facility arrests. Higher here: the national passport lock-out, entry refusal, and a lifetime fraud route. Lower: no death-penalty or capital pathway and a stronger anti-discrimination base.

Similar: universal document-based entry exposure and routine refusal. Higher here: no documented exclusion register and no broad refusal practice. Lower: the dossier documents custody abuse and criminal trespass, which 0.35-A does not.

Lower: the dossier documents custody harm and arrest, which 0.45-D lacks. Similar in universal-exposure tier: registration-based exposure at the border and facilities. Higher: 0.45-D has a registration database and no documented custody sexual abuse.

parsed.synthesis: National document rules, entry refusal and facility restrictions in roughly 19 states form a universal exposure every visitor carries. The arrest and birth-sex custody placement, plus documented custody abuse in immigration and federal corrections, make the consequences after discovery severe. State minor-care bans and federal counterterrorism framing add exposure. Partial protections (national hate-crime and employment law, anti-discrimination in 22 states plus DC, courts enjoining some orders) do not offset the documented state-imposed rules. Violence is undocumented on a rate basis. No execution or capital pathway is documented, so the rating sits in the high-risk band, toward its upper edge.
